papers.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
papers.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, especially scATAC-seq, has been applied to map the epigenetic regulatory programs underlying bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration, and how these programs go awry in skeletal diseases. It highlights how these technologies reveal transcription factor binding and gene expression dynamics that determine bone cell fate at single-cell resolution, providing a resource for understanding skeletal biology and disease.

papers.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a focused knowledge graph that organizes Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension accompanied by anxiety, depression, or insomnia, linking syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs to their sources. It then evaluates the knowledge graph's contribution to generated answers using a blinded question-answering assessment. The work provides a structured resource and an evaluation framework for TCM knowledge retrieval in a specific comorbidity context.

papers.title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
papers.abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 w
papers.summary: This study used a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine learning to identify SNP markers associated with body weight in broiler chickens. The work demonstrates that GBS plus ensemble ML can serve as an affordable alternative to high-density SNP arrays for genome-wide association studies in poultry breeding.

papers.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
papers.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar
papers.summary: This perspective describes how the CABBI center organized a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to engineer C4 grasses (such as sugarcane, sorghum, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol oils in vegetative biomass for renewable fuels and biobased chemicals. It highlights the need to coordinate molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program, and distills lessons from applying this integrated approach across multiple feedstocks. The paper serves as a roadmap for multidisciplinary bioenergy crop engineering rather than reporting a single new experimental result.

papers.title: Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.
papers.abstract: Model organisms carry decades of systematic gene-phenotype annotation, but connecting those annotations to human disease is rarely straightforward. Phenologs offer a principled way to bridge this gap. A human disease and a model-organism phenotype are phenologs when their associated genes, linked by orthology, overlap more than expected by chance, so the genes of one become candidates for the other. Here we compute phenologs from the Monarch Knowledge Graph, which integrates gene-disease, gene-phenotype and orthology data for human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as ort
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors compute phenologs—pairs of human diseases and model-organism phenotypes whose associated genes overlap more than expected by chance after orthology mapping—at knowledge-graph scale using the Monarch Knowledge Graph, covering human and seven model species. Using PANTHER protein families as orthology groups, they produce a catalog of candidate human disease genes derived from mouse-to-slime-mold phenotype annotations for thousands of diseases. This provides a systematic, principled resource for cross-species gene discovery in human disease.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that converts literature on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, traceable evidence records. Each finding is linked to its source text and normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, making dispersed surveillance, epidemiological, and genomic evidence reusable and auditable.

papers.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware transformer model to predict the onset of acute kidney injury and forecast patient prognosis using longitudinal electronic health record data. The approach addresses the high dimensionality and temporal complexity of EHRs, aiming to support earlier prevention and better post-onset care decisions.

papers.title: Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.
papers.abstract: Psychiatric diagnostic practice faces persistent challenges in adequately capturing the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders. Conventional categorical classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) rely on rigid symptom-based criteria that often fail to represent multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and high rates of comorbidity. Although dimensional models, domain-specific ontologies, and alternative taxonomi
papers.summary: This paper develops a Meta Mesh Ontology designed to integrate mental health knowledge across different domains, addressing the limitations of rigid categorical systems like DSM-5 and ICD-11. The ontology aims to capture the multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and comorbidity patterns that conventional diagnostic criteria often miss. The study includes development and evaluation of the ontology's ability to support cross-domain knowledge integration in psychiatry.

papers.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications,
papers.summary: scSpatial is a new atlas/database that consolidates single-cell spatial omics datasets that were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and characterization of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the spatial omics community.

papers.title: AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance.
papers.abstract: Biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on heterogeneous data sources, yet differences in data structure, terminology, evidence quality, and provenance complicate their integration into reliable knowledge resources. Here, we develop an evidence-aware framework for processing and integrating heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data from FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records in Mass General Brigham. The framework combines large language model (LLM)-based information extraction, ontology-driven sem
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present an evidence-aware AI framework that integrates heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data—FAERS reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and EHRs—using LLM-based information extraction and ontology-driven semantic integration. This enables more reliable knowledge discovery for drug safety surveillance by accounting for differences in data structure, terminology, and evidence quality across sources.

papers.title: The Drosophila Secretome.
papers.abstract: Secreted proteins are synthesized within the cell and actively transported outside, where they contribute to development, physiology, immunity, and cell-cell communication. In Drosophila melanogaster , many secreted proteins are evolutionarily conserved, making this species a powerful model for studying human development, cancer, neurobiology, and immune regulation. To assemble the Drosophila secretome, we systematically analyzed all fly protein sequences with computational tools, integrating FlyBase, UniProt and Gene Ontology annotations, and incorporating large-scale proteomics datasets. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a systematic computational assembly of the Drosophila secretome by analyzing all fly protein sequences with prediction tools and integrating FlyBase, UniProt, Gene Ontology annotations, and large-scale proteomics data. The resulting resource catalogs secreted proteins in the fly, many of which are conserved in humans, supporting Drosophila as a model for development, cancer, neurobiology, and immunity. It provides a community resource for identifying and studying secreted proteins.

papers.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconcep
papers.summary: This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary advice to individuals using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—has advanced rapidly in discovery but lags in clinical translation because evidence is fragmented across life stages and poorly integrated with systems biology. The authors call for a lifespan-oriented framework that accounts for how nutritional needs and response heterogeneity change from preconception onward.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
papers.abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporati
papers.summary: gcPathogen 2.0 is a major update to a pathogen genomics database, expanding coverage from 1,134 to 1,506 pathogenic species across bacteria, fungi, viruses, and parasites, with over 2.3 million genomic records. The update adds transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution to support One Health research, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides. It is designed to address analytical bottlenecks in global pathogen surveillance by integrating multi-omics data.

papers.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7  756  867 reference spectra ass
papers.summary: Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that supports standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows. It contains over 7.7 million reference spectra, making it a large-scale resource for metabolomics data reuse and analysis.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized agents over heterogeneous biological data. It aims to reduce the fragmentation of specialized tools by letting users interact in natural language while the agents handle network-driven analysis. The work is presented as a platform development study, emphasizing workflow integration rather than a specific biological discovery.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, achieving extensive coverage of UniProtKB, and includes mappings to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein functional annotation across biology.

papers.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
papers.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed
papers.summary: This study profiled miRNA expression changes in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells after 24-hour exposure to crystalline silica particles, examining both intracellular and extracellular (secreted) miRNAs alongside cytotoxicity. The work identifies silica-responsive miRNA signatures that could serve as candidate effect biomarkers for exposure biomonitoring in occupational settings. Findings are preliminary and cell-line based, requiring validation in human samples.

papers.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on symptom management for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a knowledge graph intended to guide nursing interventions. The work addresses the lack of structured clinical tools for managing GVHD's multi-organ symptoms by organizing existing evidence into a navigable knowledge map. It is a nursing informatics contribution rather than a primary data or methods study.

papers.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs
papers.summary: This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of the skin bacterium Cutibacterium acnes trigger neutrophils and Th17 T cells to release extracellular traps (web-like DNA structures). While neutrophil traps looked the same regardless of bacterial strain, T-cell traps induced by the two strains had distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences. This links a common skin commensal to immune cell trap formation with potential relevance to acne pathogenesis.

papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reconceived not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this reframing, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic drug-development models are built and parameterized.

papers.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
papers.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to PDB structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the previous internal PDBe pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast scalable sequence search, a better bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity. This makes high-quality structure-sequence integration accessible to any lab without relying on proprietary infrastructure.

papers.title: EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.
papers.abstract: Functional enrichment of transcriptomic datasets can be constrained by incomplete annotation, uneven identifier recognition, and uncertainty about which organism annotation resource provides the most informative functional context. EchoGO is a reproducible downstream framework that retains target GOseq enrichment as the primary functional evidence while evaluating the same transcriptomic response across researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. Evidence is assembled at the GO-term level with its analytical and organism provenance, allowing research
papers.summary: EchoGO is a reproducible framework for functional enrichment of transcriptomic data that keeps GOseq as the primary evidence while cross-checking the same gene response against multiple researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. It assembles evidence at the GO-term level with analytical and organism provenance, helping address incomplete annotation and uneven identifier recognition. The tool is aimed at making downstream functional interpretation more transparent and reproducible.

papers.title: Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states.
papers.abstract: Human performance often fails not because latent capacity is absent, but because access to high-functioning cognitive states is unstable under fatigue, distraction, overload, and pressure. This hypothesis paper proposes closed-loop cognitive state control-informally, supercognition-as a neuroengineering objective: rapid entry into, stabilization of, and recovery of an individual's highest available task-specific cognitive state. The framework treats cognition as a partially observable dynamical system whose latent states would be inferred from multimodal behavioral, physiological, contextual,
papers.summary: This hypothesis paper proposes a framework for 'closed-loop cognitive state control,' in which an individual's task-specific high-performance cognitive states are rapidly entered, stabilized, and recovered. Cognition is modeled as a partially observable dynamical system whose latent states would be inferred in real time from multimodal behavioral, physiological, and contextual signals, enabling adaptive neuroengineering interventions. The work is conceptual and does not present empirical validation.

papers.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. Here, we present HuRInterDB (Human lncRNA-Protein Interaction Database), a comprehensive and standardized database that focuses on human lncRNA-protein in
papers.summary: HuRInterDB is a new standardized database that consolidates human lncRNA-protein interaction records scattered across multiple public databases, addressing the fragmentation that complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. It provides a comprehensive resource for exploring the landscape of lncRNA-protein interactions, which are key to understanding lncRNA regulatory functions.

papers.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning m
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-generated predictions of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities are often conflated with experimentally validated ones, and that this distinction should be treated as a central methodological problem rather than an afterthought. It surveys how machine learning and genome-scale systems biology generate metabolic hypotheses at scale, and discusses what evidence is needed to move from computational prediction to confirmed synthetic lethal targets.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
papers.abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. With strengths in multi-omics integration, complex pattern recognition, and
papers.summary: This review argues that AI can serve as an integrated toolkit across the antibacterial drug discovery pipeline, from target identification and hit discovery to resistance prediction and translational decision-making. It frames AI's value around multi-omics integration and complex pattern recognition to address diverse resistance mechanisms and the slow pace of conventional antibiotic development. The paper is largely conceptual and strategic, aiming to define where and how AI should be applied rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health.
papers.abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. This Perspective proposes sustainable nutrition as a unifying concept: maintaining nutritional status that supports growth, development, and health across the lifespan while accounting for population needs, context, and the capacity and resilience
papers.summary: This perspective proposes 'sustainable nutrition' as a unifying concept that links dietary intake and health outcomes with food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. It argues that advancing public and planetary health requires understanding nutrition within these broader food-system and environmental contexts rather than focusing on nutrients and physiology alone.
